units.function: Route tests for validating Agent Adapter types and applying Codex-local credential/home isolation defaults during Agent create and update.
units.dependencyDirection: Agent routes validate the requested type against the active server Adapter registry, transform Adapter config, invoke SecretService/env-binding and instructions helpers, then pass normalized configuration to AgentService persistence.
units.keyDataModels: Agent Adapter type/config, environment map, OPENAI_API_KEY, CODEX_HOME, dynamically registered Adapter and per-Company/per-Agent isolated Codex home path.
units.lifecycle: A dynamically registered external Adapter type can create an Agent, while an unregistered arbitrary string is rejected. Keyless Codex Agents do not receive an injected API key or home on create/update. Supplying a per-Agent OpenAI key automatically selects an isolated Company/Agent Codex home. Callers may also explicitly point a Codex Agent at the host user's shared ~/.codex home.
units.testAssessment: Seven focused route cases cover dynamic/unknown types and the main keyless/keyed create/update home behaviors. Missing are proof that plaintext keys are converted to SecretRef before persistence/logging, path traversal/symlink/ownership/mode checks, cross-Company home reuse, concurrent Agent creation, key removal/rotation, non-OpenAI secrets, shared-home authorization warnings, managed-cloud prohibition, audit receipts and actual filesystem/runtime isolation. Extensive mocks mean database and SecretService guarantees are not exercised.
units.designRationale: Keep Adapter validation extensible while preventing an Agent-specific API key from contaminating or reading the host user's Codex login by default; retain a convenience path for local users who intentionally want to reuse their existing Codex authentication.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must let many vendor-neutral Connectors coexist without inheriting a developer's personal credentials, configuration, sessions or filesystem state, and must keep enterprise secrets and execution identities isolated by tenant and Connector instance.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT registry-backed type validation and automatic per-Connector credential-home isolation. Persist only SecretRef bindings, enforce execution-node-owned private directories and verify permissions. REJECT host ~/.codex sharing as a production/default feature; if retained for single-user local development, gate it behind a deployment-profile policy, explicit high-risk acknowledgement, no enterprise data and a visible non-production status.
units.responsibilityConflict: Sharing the host Codex home can cause an Agent to act with a real person's login, private sessions and ambient authority while the control plane attributes work to a different responsible user. The tests accept plaintext OPENAI_API_KEY in route configuration and mock away persistence normalization, so they do not prove credential custody, redaction or accountable approval.
